title: A Dataset Showing a Century of Evolution in the Complexity of the United States Legal Code
summary: A century-scale dataset combines U.S. Code text and cross-references from 1926–2023 with hierarchical structure from 1994 onward. It supports longitudinal analysis of legal growth, organization, and interdependence.

figure.alt: Workflow connecting historical U.S. Code volumes and GovInfo records to text statistics, hierarchical trees, and cross-reference networks.
figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: From historical legal text to three complementary views of the U.S. Code.

title: Scaling laws for function diversity and specialization across socioeconomic and biological complex systems
summary: Functional diversity grows sublinearly with size across biological and organizational systems, while cities follow a logarithmic pattern. A two-parameter model links these regularities to diversification and specialization.

figure.alt: Six plots compare function diversity and abundance distributions in bacterial and archaeal cells, federal agencies, and metropolitan areas.
figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: How functional variety and specialization change with system size.

title: When Common Law Ages: Two Centuries of Growing Inertia in US Judicial Opinions
summary: Citation patterns across nearly four million U.S. judicial opinions reveal a long-run decline in disruption of established precedent, with variation across courts. The study examines how the accumulation of case law relates to this growing inertia.

figure.alt: Time series of average citation-based disruption for all U.S. cases, state cases, and federal cases, with separate supreme-court trends.
figure.label: Figure 2
figure.caption: Long-run decline in citation-based disruption, with differences across court systems.

title: Bottom-up systems at scale: The case of Reddit
summary: Across Reddit communities, discussion and comment removal grow faster than active membership, while automated oversight scales approximately linearly. Substantial differences remain after accounting for size, revealing distinct regulatory profiles.

figure.alt: Scaling plots compare comments, removed comments, and bot comments with active users; time series show changes in removal activity and its scaling exponent.
figure.label: Figure 2
figure.caption: Community size and three forms of activity: discussion, enforcement, and bot oversight.

title: A generative model of function growth explains hidden self-similarities across biological and social systems
summary: A generalized Yule–Simon model explains how new functions and preferential growth jointly shape diversity and abundance. Rescaling rank by functional diversity reveals shared patterns within prokaryotes, federal agencies, and cities.

figure.alt: Normalized rank-frequency curves for prokaryotes, federal agencies, and cities align within each class after rank is rescaled by functional diversity.
figure.label: Figure 6
figure.caption: Rescaling functional ranks reveals similarities hidden by differences in system size.

title: Three Centuries of the Laws of Cricket Reveal Core Principles of the Evolution of Regulatory Mechanisms
summary: A dataset spanning 268 years tracks how cricket’s rules expand and become more hierarchical and interconnected. The analysis relates textual growth to accumulated matches and traces a shift in regulatory emphasis toward officiating.

figure.alt: A timeline of cricket rule changes accompanies charts of the number of Laws, structural depth, word count, and rule-tree leaves over time.
figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Nearly three centuries of changes in the size and structure of cricket’s rules.

title: What makes Individual I's a Collective We; Coordination mechanisms & costs
summary: Wikipedia projects face different coordination costs as they grow: discussion and reverts increase faster than membership, while administrator and bot activity increase more slowly. A model links these patterns to modular interactions and emerging hierarchy.

figure.alt: A coordination diagram and scaling plots compare administrator activity, talk pages, bots, and reverts as Wikipedia contributor counts increase.
figure.label: Figure 2
figure.caption: Different coordination mechanisms carry different costs as collaborative groups grow.
